idiom_name: enum Phase { case draft, published(version: Int) } + switch
implementation_notes: Swift enums carry associated values and switching over them must be exhaustive, so the state set is closed at compile time and each state holds its own payload without a class per state; this is what replaces the State protocol plus concrete classes. Transitions are value assignments on the owning struct or class, and behaviour lives either in methods that switch on the state or in the state's didSet hook. Choose a protocol plus classes when states must be extended by other modules or need reference semantics for observation.
pitfalls: A default arm (or @unknown default for a non-frozen enum) discards the exhaustiveness guarantee; keeping the enum in-module preserves it.
Enums are value types: transitioning a copy leaves the original unchanged, so mutate through the owning instance, not a local let.
Persisting the state with String(describing:) loses associated values on restore; use Codable or a separate stable code.

variants.name: GameplayKit GKStateMachine with GKState subclasses
variants.implementation_notes: Apple's GameplayKit ships the pattern as a framework: each state subclasses GKState, isValidNextState(_:) declares the legal successors, didEnter(from:) and willExit(to:) are the entry and exit hooks, and GKStateMachine(states:) owns the current state while exposing enter(_:), canEnterState(_:) and update(deltaTime:). The framework keeps the graph and the per-frame update loop explicit, which suits games and simulations; it is reference-based and Objective-C visible, so it does not compose with Swift value-semantics enums and it is only available on Apple platforms.
pitfalls: enter(_:) returns false for an illegal transition instead of throwing; ignoring the result silently keeps the old state active.
Per-state logic only runs when the owner forwards update(deltaTime:), so a forgotten call stops the machine without an error.
GKState instances are reference types shared for the machine's lifetime and must not hold per-entity data - keep that in a component.
